title: Memory and Allocation
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of memory and allocation using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates memory and allocation.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Memory and Allocation** as part of **Software Engineering, Security, and Performance**. Measure a reproducible workload before optimizing, and compare correctness plus CPU, memory, allocation, and target-specific costs. Use the subtopics—Object Allocation and Lifetime, Copying, Boxing, and Allocation Costs, Garbage Collection on the JVM—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it

items.title: Object Allocation and Lifetime
items.text: Object Allocation and Lifetime should be evaluated against input size, allocation behavior, and workload. Start with a correctness test and reproducible measurement; choose the simplest implementation that meets the requirement.

items.title: Garbage Collection on the JVM
items.text: Garbage Collection on the JVM is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
